senses.sense_definition: An apparently self-contradictory statement that seems to be both true and false at the same time.

examples.text: The statement that this sentence is false is a classic <w>paradox</w>.
He enjoyed exploring the <w>paradox</w> of a statement that denies its own truth.

senses.sense_definition: A situation or outcome that seems contrary to common sense or expectation.

examples.text: It is a <w>paradox</w> that drinking more water can sometimes make you feel thirstier.
The <w>paradox</w> of modern life is that we are more connected yet feel more isolated.

senses.sense_definition: A person or thing that possesses contradictory qualities or features.

examples.text: She is a <w>paradox</w> because she is both extremely shy and a talented public speaker.
The politician was a <w>paradox</w> who supported policies that hurt his own voters.

senses.sense_definition: A difficult puzzle or an unanswerable question that may reveal a deeper truth.

examples.text: The philosopher spent his life trying to solve the <w>paradox</w> of human existence.
They discussed the <w>paradox</w> of how one can be both young and old at once.

senses.sense_definition: A therapeutic technique of giving instructions that are the opposite of the desired outcome to encourage change.

examples.text: The therapist used a <w>paradox</w> to help the patient overcome their fear of failure.
By using a <w>paradox</w>, the counselor forced the client to confront their own resistance.
